title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 36-38): Grothendieck is computing the automorphisms u of the profinite fundamental groupoid of the projective line minus {0,1,∞}. The groupoid is taken on several base points, and he requires u to commute with complex conjugation σ_∞ (and to be compatible with the order-3 symmetry ρ). The base points come from a symmetric cell decomposition of the Riemann sphere. The real circle cuts the sphere into two hemispheres ω, ω' (upper and lower half-planes). P^ω is the centre of hemisphere ω, plausibly the ρ-fixed point e^{±iπ/3}. Q_i (i = 1,2,3) are points on the three real intervals. R_i^ω are further points in each hemisphere. The figure shows a sphere with six meridians, the equator, and arrows. The parameters are triples of elements of π̂_{0,3} = π̂_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}): λ, η, ξ, and the derived α', β', ξ'. These say how u acts on chosen generating paths (formulas 54, 57, 63-65 on p. 36).

On this page:
(67) For the composite path d̃_i^ω : P^ω → R_i^{ω'}, which runs through Q_{ωi} (p. 36, formula 66), u acts by left multiplication: u(d̃_i^ω) = φ_i^ω(ξ') d̃_i^ω, with ξ' = ηξ written underneath. This gives a 'geometric' meaning to the auxiliary parameter ξ'.
(66') He introduces the paths d_i^ω = c^{ω'}_{ω'i} · d^ω_{ω'i} : P^ω → Q_{ω'i} → R_i^ω. Note that τ (conjugation) sends d_i^ω to d_i^{ω'}.
(67') He states an analogous formula for u(d_i^ω); its argument is illegible.

He then lists two further subgroupoids of the large groupoid VI:
- VII is the full subgroupoid on the eight vertices R_i^ω, P^ω (6 + 2). It is generated by the 24 arrows d_i'^ω, d_i^ω, a_i^ω, b_i^ω (4 types × 3 values of i × 2 hemispheres).
- The full subgroupoid on Q_i, P^ω is essentially the groupoid IV already treated, but presented by a slightly larger graph on six vertices.

In VII only the d_i^ω are distinguished, and the ã_i^ω are not added as extra data. This is legitimate by (37), because the datum α̃ governing u(ã_i^ω) already follows from ξ, which governs u(d̃_i^ω). Figures: VII is the sphere with meridians and equator; VIII = IV is a sphere with three marked points.

The next page assembles the inclusion diagram (68) of the graphs I-VII. It then shows that the vertex-fixing automorphisms of VII commuting with σ_∞ are parametrized by (λ, β', ξ') with relations: β' = α'σ_∞(λ), and β'σ_∞(β') = 1 (a 2-cycle relation). For II the relations are α'ρ(α')ρ²(α') = 1 (a 3-cycle relation) with β' = ησ_∞(η)^{-1}; he remarks that some parameters are redundant.

Purpose: this is a hands-on derivation of the relations defining the Grothendieck-Teichmüller-type group acting on the genus-0, four-point level. It uses many base points ('tangential'/symmetric points) and a cell decomposition of the sphere, with real structure. In substance these are the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations of Drinfeld's GT, formulated here groupoid-theoretically before Drinfeld (1990).
errors: The argument of φ_i^ω in (67') is illegible and possibly unfinished. Only (67) is clearly established on this page.

The superscript/subscript conventions for composite paths are not consistent between (66) and (66'): c^ω_{ωi}·d^ω_{ωi} versus c^{ω'}_{ω'i}·d^ω_{ω'i}. With paths from P^ω, the intermediate point and the target hemisphere interchange. This is plausible given the geometry but is not checked on the page.
The count '24 flèches' for VII is consistent (4 types × 3 × 2). The 'six sommets' presentation of IV is asserted without listing the arrows.
No real errors are visible. The page is bookkeeping toward the relations on p. 38.

ideas.what: Computing automorphisms of the profinite fundamental groupoid of P^1−{0,1,∞} on a symmetric set of several base points, using a cell decomposition of the sphere (hemispheres, real intervals) and compatibility with complex conjugation.
ideas.modern_name: Groupoid approach to the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group / tangential base points; GT action on π̂_1 of M_{0,4}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990, GT-hat); Ihara; Deligne (1989, tangential base points); Lochak-Schneps for the groupoid formulation
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984): Teichmüller tower, groupoids with base points stable under symmetries, the program of determining the Galois action by levels 1 and 2. The detailed computations are not published.

ideas.what: Encoding u by parameters in π̂_{0,3} attached to generating paths (u(d̃) = φ(ξ')d̃), and reducing the parameters via relations (2-cycle β'σ_∞(β') = 1; 3-cycle α'ρ(α')ρ²(α') = 1).
ideas.modern_name: The (λ, f) parametrization of GT-hat with the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations

ideas.what: Comparing presentations of the same groupoid by different generating graphs (IV versus a six-vertex graph; full subgroupoids VII ⊂ VI), with an inclusion diagram of graphs.
ideas.modern_name: Presentations of fundamental groupoids on several base points; change of base-point sets

missed.claim: This page and its neighbours contain a pre-1990 explicit computation, by Grothendieck, of the relations governing automorphisms of the profinite π_1-groupoid of P^1−{0,1,∞} with real structure. These are essentially Drinfeld's 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations. They are set up via a symmetric multi-base-point groupoid with explicit generating graphs I-VII. The historical record mostly credits the explicit relations to Drinfeld and Ihara; the Esquisse states only the program.
missed.quote: Je vois encore deux cas à regarder, savoir le sous-groupoïde plein de VI induit sur les huit sommets (R_{iω}, P^ω), soit VII
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's priority-level engagement with the GT relations. The systematic use of conjugation-equivariant groupoids on many base points (graphs I-VII) may be a variant of the real/'σ_∞-equivariant' GT not fully worked out in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is technical bookkeeping: path definitions and listing subgroupoids. Its interest lies in the surrounding computation, which shows Grothendieck explicitly deriving GT-type relations with complex-conjugation equivariance. This is broadly known to exist through his Esquisse and archive studies, so it is notable but not shocking.
transcription_corrections: Next-page 'respire les u(ã_i^ω)' should almost certainly read 'régit les u(ã_i^ω)', and likewise 'qui régit les u(d̃_i^ω)'. The sentence is: '(Dans (37), la donnée de α̃, qui régit les u(ã_i^ω), résulte déjà de celle de ξ, qui régit les u(d̃_i^ω))'.
'(R_{iω}, P^ω)' should be read as the vertices R_i^ω, P^ω.
'mais [?] les = sommets' is likely 'mais avec les = sommets' (the doubled vertices), followed by 'représenté par un graphe un peu plus grand' with 'six' inserted.
In (66') the margin figure shows P^ω → Q_{ω'i} via d^ω_{ω'i}, then c^{ω'}_{ω'i} to R_i^ω. The arrow from P^ω to R_i^ω is dashed.
The argument of (67') is illegible. It appears to involve η, ξ' and ξ (something like φ_i^ω(η(ξ'ξ))) and should not be transcribed as η·ξ with confidence.
